en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Nighttime Darkness 17.
The Training Rule on Spreading Out Without Asking for Permission.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

Now at that time, a number of bhikkhunīs were traveling from the Kosala country toward Sāvatthī. Having arrived at a certain village in the evening, they approached a certain brahmin family and requested lodging.
Then that brahmin woman said to those bhikkhunīs, "Wait, noble ladies, until the brahmin returns."
The bhikkhunīs, thinking, "Until the brahmin arrives," spread out the bedding; some sat down and some lay down.
Then that brahmin, having arrived at night, said this to the brahmin woman:
“Who are these? “They are bhikkhunīs, noble sir.
“Drive these shaven-headed harlots out! he had them driven out from the house.
Then those bhikkhunīs went to Sāvatthī and reported this matter to the bhikkhunīs.
Those bhikkhunīs who were few in desires... [as before]... complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
"How can these bhikkhunīs, having approached families at an improper time, spread out a bed and sit down or lie down without asking permission from the owners?"... [as before]...
“Is it true, monks, that nuns indeed visit families at an improper time, and having spread out a bed without asking the owners’ permission, sit down upon it and lie down upon it?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them … [as before] …
"How indeed, monks, could bhikkhunīs, having approached families at an improper time, spread out a bed and sit down or lie down there without asking the owners for permission?
This, monks, does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...

And so, monks, let the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule: ‘If a bhikkhunī, having approached a family at an improper time, spreads out a bed and sits down or lies down there without asking the owners for permission, that is an offense of wrong-doing.’"

“Whatever nun, having approached families at an improper time, should spread out a bed or have one spread out, and sit down or lie down upon it without having asked permission from the owner, that is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
“Whatever nun” means whichever nun of such a kind... [and so forth].
"Bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the type of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"Improper time" (vikāla) means:
From sunset until sunrise.
As for "family," there are four families: the khattiya family, the brāhmaṇa family, the vessa family, and the sudda family.
"Having approached" means having gone there.
"Without asking the owners" means...
Without having asked the person who is the master of that family and authorized to give;
"a bed" means even as much as a mat made of leaves.
"Having spread" means having spread it oneself.
"Having had it spread" means...
Having had another mat spread out.
"Should sit down" means:
if she sits down on that [mat], there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
"Should lie down":
if she lies down upon it, there is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*).

If, not having asked permission, she perceives that she has not asked permission, and having spread out the bed herself or having had it spread out, she sits down or lies down upon it, there is an offense of expiation.

If she spreads out a bed or has one spread out, or sits down or lies down upon it without having asked permission, and she is in doubt [as to whether she asked], there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If she spreads out a bed or has one spread out, or sits down or lies down upon it without having asked permission, while perceiving that she did ask permission, there is an offense of expiation.
If she asks permission but perceives that she did not ask permission, there is an offense of wrongdoing (dukkaṭa).
If she has asked for permission but is in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If she has asked for permission and perceives that she has asked for permission, there is no offense.
There is no offense—
If, having asked for permission, one spreads out a bed or has it spread out, and then sits down on it or lies down on it—
unless one is ill or in cases of emergency.
"In the case of one who is insane,
or in the case of one who is a first-offender.
The seventh training rule is concluded.
